title: Orchestrator Mode Switch 2026-06-19
purpose: Create one deterministic orchestrator-mode switch that configures the effective pager route, tmux monitor target, and the matching Codex or Claude autoping surface for whichever tool is the active main session. Implementer/reviewer role selection stays independent and remains handled by the existing role switch.
evidence_command: PYTHONHASHSEED=0 python3 -m pytest -q mu/tests/tools/test_orchestrator_mode_switch.py mu/tests/tools/test_set_roles.py mu/tests/tools/test_codex_startup_state.py mu/tests/tools/test_pipeline_monitor_autofollow.py --tb=short && PYTHONHASHSEED=0 python3 -m pytest -q tests/tools/test_commit_executor_post_merge_cleanup.py -k growth_cap && python3 mu/tools/checks/check_host_semantics_ratchet.py
evidence_delta: (1) A single command applies orchestrator mode codex|claude: effective pager route matches the selected orchestrator without rewriting the shipped tracked pager default, stale opposite-orchestrator pending pager targets are cleared or terminally skipped, monitor/autoping restart arguments point at the selected live root and bus, and the wrong orchestrator autoping surface is stopped or reported. (2) The command can dry-run/show, apply, and verify without launching real Claude, Codex, or tmux in tests. (3) The switch is deterministic and idempotent across main and linked worktrees while preserving independent implementer/reviewer role_agents. (4) Verification fails if a live bridge-agent subprocess exists but tmux Who's Working is blank, labels live Codex as Claude, classifies review as implement because bridge_supervisor options precede the review subcommand, leaves stale opposite-orchestrator pager work pending, or uses Claude as a generic operator-facing name for a Codex-run request/worker.
progress_proof_before: During the 2026-06-19 session, Codex implementer/reviewer processes were live but tmux displayed Claude or blank Who's Working because role labels, orchestrator wiring, compatibility field names, and live subprocess provider detection were conflated; pager state tried route=both and hit Claude limits; Codex autoping was rooted at the stale main `.agent_bus` instead of the live lane bus. Fixing it required several manual process searches.
progress_proof_after: One command puts an operator session into the chosen orchestrator mode and verifies the effective state: effective pager route matches codex or claude, stale opposite-orchestrator pager backlog cannot spawn new wakeups, tmux panes use the current autofollow/live root, Who's Working reports the live subprocess provider/role from process truth, selected request/worker labels are neutral and registry-derived rather than Claude-generic, the selected orchestrator autoping watcher is pinned to the selected root/bus/session id, the opposite autoping surface is absent, implementer/reviewer roles are preserved, and model/display strings come from one config source.
scope_summary: Pipeline/operator tooling only: deterministic orchestrator-mode switch for pager, tmux monitor, and autoping. Do not touch runtime, substrate, seed, StructuralNumbers, arithmetic gates, or role-pin/observability wave implementation files beyond shared helper reuse if unavoidable. Do not couple orchestrator mode to implementer/reviewer role selection.

mu/tools/executors/executor_config.json bridge_agent_defaults (READ OR PROMOTE) -- use as the single provider/model/display registry, or migrate it to a dedicated models.json with compatibility reads; do not duplicate model/display strings in the switch.
mu/tools/observability/pipeline_agent_pager.py (MODIFY) -- read bus-local orchestrator mode as the effective pager route ahead of the shipped tracked default.
mu/tools/session/ensure_codex_autoping.sh (MODIFY IF NEEDED) -- expose/reuse deterministic Codex watcher restart behavior for a selected root and bus.
mu/tools/session/ensure_claude_autoping.sh (MODIFY IF NEEDED) -- expose/reuse deterministic Claude watcher restart behavior for a selected root and bus.
mu/tools/observability/pipeline_monitor.sh (MODIFY IF NEEDED) -- expose/reuse deterministic tmux rebuild/autofollow behavior for the selected orchestrator session.

mu/tools/observability/_pane_processes.sh and _pane_timeline.sh (MODIFY/VERIFY) -- the switch verification must prove monitor panes identify live bridge-agent workers from process truth, not stale role defaults.

mu/tools/executors/launch_wave.py and routing-record helpers (MODIFY IF NEEDED) -- expose a neutral request field/name for operator-facing output; keep any request_for_claude compatibility path parse-only until downstream callers migrate.

work_items: Design the user-facing command name and options so the operator can run one simple command for the active orchestrator: --mode codex|claude, --repo-root, --bus-dir, --tmux-session, dry-run/show, apply, and verify.
Keep mu/tools/executors/set_roles.py as the separate implementer/reviewer role switch. The orchestrator switch must not write role_agents, backends, or bridge_reviewers.

Reuse the repo's single provider/model/display source. Prefer executor_config.json.bridge_agent_defaults; if that shape is too role-specific, create a small models.json/provider registry and update existing readers to consume it through one compatibility helper.
Set the bus-local orchestrator mode so pager events use the selected orchestrator as the effective route while preserving the shipped executor_config.json default; do not require manual JSON editing.

When switching away from an orchestrator, deterministically clear or terminally skip stale pending pager targets for the opposite orchestrator. A prior route=both event must not keep launching forbidden claude -p or codex exec resume wakeups after the route has been switched.

Make tmux/autoping handling deterministic: stop the opposite orchestrator's autoping surface, ensure exactly one selected-orchestrator watcher for the selected root/bus/session id, and rebuild or refresh tmux monitor with autofollow/live-root settings.

Add a verification subcommand or post-apply check that prints effective orchestrator mode, effective pager route, live root/bus, active autoping watcher path, current role_agents for visibility only, whether the wrong orchestrator's pager/autoping process remains, whether stale opposite-orchestrator pager targets remain pending, and whether tmux Who's Working has a nonblank live-worker line when a bridge-agent subprocess is running.

Fix or gate the pane-worker detector so it uses live subprocess truth and the provider registry. A live codex exec -m gpt-5.5 process must display as Codex even when role_agents.implementer is Claude, and a bridge supervisor command with global options before the review subcommand must still classify the worker as reviewing.
Remove bounded PID truncation that hides the relevant worker when more than five global Codex/Claude processes exist; prefer filtering by repo root before limiting rendered rows.

Neutralize Claude-named generic request surfaces in launcher/routing/tmux/pager output. If the schema still accepts request_for_claude for compatibility, it must be documented as deprecated parse-only compatibility and must not make a Codex-run wave display as Claude.
Document how to switch orchestrator mode separately from switching implementer/reviewer roles, and document where model/provider strings live.
Keep test coverage fake-process/fake-tmux based; do not launch real Codex, Claude, or persistent tmux windows in tests.
Run the configured evidence command and collect the indicator artifact.
constraints: Use the pipeline launcher and dispatcher path for this wave when launched.
Support both Codex and Claude as orchestrator modes, but tests must not require a live Claude or Codex session.
Do not touch runtime, substrate, seed, registry, projection seed, JS parity, StructuralNumbers, arithmetic gates, or GCD/rational wave files.
Do not duplicate the separate role-pin launcher wave; this switch changes orchestrator pager/autoping/tmux wiring, not implementer/reviewer roles.
Do not bind role_agents to orchestrator mode. Claude can be orchestrator while Codex is implementer/reviewer, and Codex can be orchestrator while Claude or Codex are selected pipeline roles.

Do not hardcode Codex/Claude model names, effort levels, or display names outside the single provider/model registry. If Codex or Claude model names change, one JSON edit must update switch output, tmux labels, and pager/autoping command construction where those fields apply.
Do not allow role defaults to override live process identity in tmux panes. Orchestrator mode, role_agents, and live subprocess provider are distinct facts and must be reported distinctly.
Do not allow compatibility field names such as request_for_claude to become operator-facing truth for Codex-run waves.
The command must be idempotent and safe to run repeatedly.
stop_conditions: Stop done when one deterministic command covers the effective orchestrator pager route, tmux, and selected Codex/Claude autoping behavior while preserving independent roles, evidence passes, docs are updated, and the indicator artifact is collected.
Halt as NEEDS_RESCOPING if the implementation requires broad monitor redesign beyond a deterministic switch wrapper.
Halt as POLICY_BOUND if tests require launching real Claude or modifying hidden personal state.
Do not commit without a real handoff artifact and gate-green evidence.
acceptance_criteria: One command can switch orchestrator mode to codex or claude without changing implementer/reviewer role_agents or derived backends/bridge_reviewers.
The command sets the effective pager route to the selected orchestrator mode without rewriting the shipped tracked pager default.

The command handles stale pager backlog: after switching to Codex mode, prior route=both events cannot continue spawning Claude pager wakeups; after switching to Claude mode, prior Codex pending targets are not dispatched unless explicitly selected again.

Model, effort, and display-name metadata are read from one JSON provider registry (bridge_agent_defaults or a promoted models.json), with tests proving the switch does not duplicate stale model strings.
The command restarts/rebuilds tmux monitor/autoping for the selected live root and bus, using Codex autoping in Codex mode and Claude autoping in Claude mode.
The command verifies the final state and reports any remaining wrong-orchestrator pager/autoping process as a failure.

The command verifies pane health: if a live bridge-agent subprocess exists for the selected root/bus, Who's Working must not be blank, must not label a live Codex subprocess as Claude, and must classify review/implement from the bridge supervisor/executor parent chain even when supervisor options precede the review subcommand.

Operator-facing launcher, routing, tmux, pager, and autoping output must not use Claude as a generic name for the active worker/request. Codex implementer/reviewer runs must display as Codex; any retained request_for_claude field is compatibility input only, not display truth.
Dry-run/show mode reports the exact changes and selected root/bus without modifying files or processes.
Tests pass without launching real Codex, Claude, or persistent tmux windows.
request_for_claude: Compatibility input only: run this wave with the configured Codex implementer/reviewer roles for this run. Implement a deterministic orchestrator-mode switch that covers effective pager route, stale opposite-orchestrator pager backlog cleanup, tmux monitor, selected Codex or Claude autoping surface, and pane-health verification together, with dry-run/show/apply/verify behavior and fake-process tests. Keep implementer/reviewer roles independent; do not call set_roles.py or mutate role_agents from the orchestrator switch. The switch must fail verification when Who's Working is blank for a live bridge worker, when live Codex is labeled Claude, when stale opposite-orchestrator pager targets remain pending, when compatibility field names cause Codex work to display as Claude, or when bridge_supervisor global args before the review subcommand cause a reviewing worker to appear as implementing.
authorization_note: Founder directive 2026-06-19: stop manually searching and toggling pager/tmux/autoping surfaces; create an easy deterministic orchestrator switch while keeping implementer/reviewer role selection separate.
routing_summary: Queue deterministic orchestrator-mode switch for pager, tmux, and selected Codex/Claude autoping.
